The sensible young man resisting the GTA 6 hype

He won't be chucking a sickie on Thursday just to play a computer game.

Actual Article Body:

Two things happened in the barber's seat yesterday.

Login or signup to continue reading

The cross between Catweazle and Yahoo Serious staring back at me in the mirror - a product of months of tonsorial neglect - was transformed before my eyes.

And I learnt the young bloke performing this miracle would not be taking the day off to play Grand Theft Auto 6.

If you believe the breathless hype around the launch of this computer game, he's one of the few mainly young men who won't be chucking a sickie on Thursday.

Mainstream media has been full of reports warning of absenteeism and a slump in productivity as gamers skip work to dive into the new game.

In the US it's estimated up to 12.5 million Americans plan to take time off. There are claims GTA 6 will cost the economy billions in lost productivity. Even some military units have pre-empted an AWOL epidemic by giving their troops GTA 6 leave.

In Australia last month, the Fair Work Ombudsman took to social media to explain what was allowed under workplace law for sudden absences. Playing a new computer game wasn't on the list.

And this week a Nine sports journalist became the story when he confessed in print to booking a week of annual leave just to play GTA 6. Now middle-aged, he wrote that the GTA franchise had been with him most of his life and the wait for this iteration had been 13 years - and worth dipping into precious leave for.

That kind of obsession is puzzling even for me, who's been an on-again-off-again gamer since the 1980s. Call me old-fashioned but a week's leave is better used exploring real places rather than virtual ones on a screen in a darkened room when the sun's shining outside. Each to their own, I guess.

We'll have to wait to see if the dire predictions about so-called GTA 6 Flu come to pass.

What we do know even before it launches is the game is on track to become the biggest entertainment release in history, raking in more cash than any Hollywood blockbuster could dare to dream of. It's also sold 15 million pre-orders. At $129 for the basic game, that's a lot of money before GTA 6 is even on the shelves.

We also know there'll be hand wringing about the game's violent content and claims that it is driving...
